[[File:Ilse Fischer Oberwolfach 2026.jpg|thumb|Fischer at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2026]]
'''Ilse Fischer''' (born 29 June 1975){{r|cv}} is an Austrian mathematician whose research concerns [[enumerative combinatorics]] and [[algebraic combinatorics]], connecting these topics to [[representation theory]] and [[statistical mechanics]].{{r|as}} She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Vienna]].

==Education and career==
Fischer was born in [[Klagenfurt]]. She studied at the [[University of Vienna]] beginning in 1993, earning a master's degree (mag. rer. nat.), doctorate ([[dr. rer. nat.]]), and [[habilitation]] there respectively in 1998, 2000, and 2006.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Enumeration of perfect matchings: Rhombus tilings and Pfaffian graphs'', was jointly supervised by [[Christian Krattenthaler]] and Franz Rendl,{{r|cv|mg}} and her habilitation thesis was ''A polynomial method for the enumeration of plane partitions and alternating sign matrices''.{{r|cv}}

She worked as an assistant at [[Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt]] from 1999 to 2004,{{r|cv|start}} with a year of postdoctoral research at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2001.{{r|start}} She moved to the University of Vienna in 2004, and at Vienna she was promoted to associate professor in 2011 and to full professor in 2017.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Fischer won the 2006 Dr. Maria Schaumayer Prize,
and the 2009 [[Start-Preis]] of the [[Austrian Science Fund]].{{r|start}}

With Roger Behrend and Matjaž Konvalinka, Fischer is a winner of the 2019 [[David P. Robbins Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and [[Mathematical Association of America]], for their joint research on [[Alternating sign matrix|alternating sign matrices]].{{r|robbins}}
